points.ancienPropos: Q1 26 (06/05/2026, direct answer to a question on Type 2 retention risk, Travis Steed BofA): McEvoy asserts 'strong type 2 momentum' already at the early stage (~5% penetration) and stable group-wide retention at 90% - no specific warning signal on Type 2.
points.nouveauPropos: Q2 26 (05/08/2026): McEvoy explicitly acknowledges that management 'should have identified the Type 2 problems earlier' ('As CEO, I take accountability'), with the CFO quantifying a mechanism of degraded Type 2 retention/utilization accounting for the bulk (~2/3) of the cut to US Omnipod revenue guidance.
points.justification: Type 2 is a central growth driver of the model (anchors us_omnipod_guidance_cut_mecanisme_precise and trajectoire_2027_prudente_revisee); the shift from an explicit reassurance on the stability of retention (a question put head-on in Q1) to an admission of late detection a single quarter later is a credibility/governance signal to be tracked rather than quietly smoothed over.

clesRetenues: Q David Roman (Goldman Sachs) - review of the first year as CEO, what exceeded/met expectations: McEvoy expresses greater confidence in the growth potential, priority on corporate culture while doubling revenue (algorithms, sensor integration, international, commercial capabilities, operational scaling).

Q David Roman - confidence in the sustainability of the 20% LRT given implied high-teens H2 growth: Pease cites US/international strength, the cc FX smoothing effect, and the innovation catalysts (Libre 3 Plus, Omnipod 6, closed loop) to support 20%.

Q Robbie Marcus (JPMorgan) - how to hold 20% with a deceleration in dollars and a US exit rate below 20%: Pease points to the Omnipod 6 launch in 2027 and the full effect of the sales force expansion; McEvoy stresses the untapped market and the execution track record.

Q Robbie Marcus - assessment of market growth, seasonality drivers, new-patient performance: McEvoy notes a market acceleration in 2024-2025, Q1 weakness tied to deductible resets/ACA transitions, with month-on-month improvement through April.

Q Travis Steed (BofA) - concern over the decline in Type 2 retention, difficulty of the penetration curve ahead: McEvoy stresses strong Type 2 momentum at ~5% early penetration, the EVOLVE study (closed loop) whose enrolment has begun, Type 2 ~40% of new patients, stable group-wide retention at 90%.

Q Travis Steed - impact of seasonality on the Type 1 vs Type 2 mix: Benjamin notes ~40% Type 2 composition in new patients, similar seasonality across segments, no competitive impact from GLP-1s observed.

Q Larry Biegelsen (Wells Fargo) - how to hold 20% against an inevitable erosion of tubeless pump market share: McEvoy stresses category expansion rather than share swapping, technological lead (6th generation), manufacturing control, cost advantages.

Q Matthew O'Brien (Piper Sandler) - new pharmacy competitors disrupting Q1 patient flow: McEvoy confirms no price impact in Q1, net pricing remains positive, rational and disciplined competitive behaviour with no material market-access disruption.

Q Matthew O'Brien - impact of the product recall on new-patient acquisition: McEvoy states that the MDC did not affect Q1 new patients, rapid response with targeted corrective actions, no additional adverse events since the April 10 update.

Q Jeff Johnson (Baird) - confirmation of positive net pricing in Q1, sustainability over 2-3 years: McEvoy states positive net pricing is expected over three years, consistent with the Investor Day guidance.

Q Jeff Johnson - retention/utilization distinction for Type 2, early drop-off patterns: McEvoy/Benjamin explain that Type 2 patients require enhanced onboarding support vs Type 1; utilization stable, early-journey attrition addressed through revised engagement models.

Q Jayson Bedford (Raymond James) - drivers of the deceleration in international growth in Q2 beyond comps: Pease notes that price/mix realisation will moderate as the launches mature and the DASH->Omnipod 5 conversion stabilises, with the dollar sequence remaining positive.

Q Shagun Singh (RBC) - nature of a 10 M$ revenue shift in Q1, scope of the algorithm upgrade, pace of the sales force expansion: McEvoy details a 10 M$ inventory timing shift, the sales force building competence on the clinical message, 450K additional users via Libre 3 Plus, tripled professional training events.

Q Matt Taylor (Jefferies) - Omnipod 6 launch, share gains vs potential price/mix benefits: McEvoy positions Omnipod 6 as a category growth driver (3rd-generation algorithm, greater automation, reduced user burden, single-pod chassis simplifying prescriptions).

Q Robbie Marcus (JPMorgan) - what has changed since the ADA on Type 2 trends, when did attrition accelerate, 2027 competition/pricing assumptions: McEvoy acknowledges they should have identified the problem earlier, calls it execution not structural, retention stabilises after 90 days, corrective actions under way; Pease specifies that 2027 assumes competitive entrants and stable pricing with no retention improvement built in.

Q Travis Steed (BofA) - confidence in 2027 stabilisation, ~9% US exit rate assumption, 2027 competition assumptions: McEvoy cites early Omnipod Discover data showing that the interventions are working; Pease specifies a 9-14% range, 12% median, benefiting from product launches and the sales force expansion.

Q Larry Biegelsen (Wells Fargo) - precise Type 1 vs Type 2 retention/utilization metrics, confidence in the effectiveness of the actions: McEvoy describes differences in emotional burden, higher comorbidities, a different payer mix (60% Medicare/Medicaid), a slower insulin journey among Type 2; 10 friction points identified in the first 90 days, early improvements via Omnipod Discover.

Q Jeff Johnson (Baird) - possibility of re-engaging lapsed Type 2 patients, evidence of reversing the adherence problems, pricing assumptions tied to payer exclusions: Benjamin confirms successful re-engagement at a pilot scale now being expanded; Pease denies any pursuit of exclusive payer agreements, a disciplined pricing strategy to the benefit of the category.

Q Matt Taylor (Jefferies) - characterisation of the 90-day Type 1 vs Type 2 retention gap, early wins from the retention changes: McEvoy describes modest differences and specific friction points (insurance adjudication, first pod change, prescription pick-up); early Omnipod Discover data showing 'markedly improved' retention in limited launch.

Q Marie Thibault (BTIG) - timing of the arrival of competition, lead time before the Type 2 retention actions have a visible impact: McEvoy notes that guidance prudently assumes current trends persist through year-end without building in the benefits of the actions, with monthly monitoring of the metrics.

Q Richard Newitter (Truist) - will it be known within three months whether the initiatives are working, how quickly structural can be told apart from execution: McEvoy characterises the problem as an 'execution challenge, not structural', strong demand, programmes deployed immediately, efficiency gains offsetting the costs.

Q Joe Federico (Stifel) - return on the Type 2 investment given the shifting retention dynamics and a longer maturation cycle: McEvoy stresses the strategic importance of Type 2 (recurring revenue model, lifelong insulin dependence); Pease adds a stable acquisition cost and a continuously improving cost to serve despite the customer service expansion.

Q Kieran Ryan (Deutsche Bank) - is it mainly retention or utilization, effect of prescriber type (endo vs general practitioner) on retention: McEvoy confirms that retention is the main problem, with endocrinologists showing better retention and general practitioners requiring more confidence-building; Benjamin notes that the enlarged sales force helps serve a broader prescriber base.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Insulet is the portfolio's highest-growth medtech: 10th consecutive year above +20% cc revenue growth, FY25 closed at +30.7% with adjusted EPS $4.97 (+53%), and FY26 guided at +20-22% cc with adjusted EPS growth raised to >=30% even as the US outlook was cut. The thesis is a category-winner in insulin patch pumps (Omnipod 5) expanding into the far larger Type 2 market. Q2 crystallized the central tension: growth and margins keep beating (Q2 revenue +23.5%, adj EPS $1.66 +41.5%, adjusted OM 19.3% +140bp), but the Type 2 expansion hit its first real friction - weaker retention/utilization in the first 90 days post-onboarding, cutting US growth guidance to 17-19% and the stock by 21%. Management frames it as execution (onboarding support), not market structure; remediation pilots (Omnipod Discover: 1,600 clinicians, 12,000 patients) show early retention improvement. The first quantified 2027 indication (9-14% growth, 12% median, excluding remediation benefits) resets expectations at an intentionally beatable level.

== THESIS READ ==
- Type 2 friction is real but specific: concentrated in the first 90 days of onboarding; beyond 90 days retention stabilizes - consistent with an execution problem, not a demand problem.
- The guidance package is asymmetric: US cut, International raised (+30-32% cc), total held, EPS growth RAISED to >=30% - profitability is not the issue.
- First 2027 quantification (9-14%, median 12%) deliberately excludes remediation benefits - a conservative reset after a credibility hit.
- Balance sheet swings to net cash through the horizon; buyback boosted at FY25 results.
- Watch: 90-day retention metrics for Type 2 cohorts over the next two quarters - the single variable that arbitrates execution-vs-structure.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
None.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Base: published US GAAP in data; the thesis anchors on the company's adjusted basis for guidance comparison (management guides adjusted EPS growth). Bridge (c-ter): projections fit cleanly at a 27% normative tax with small net interest income (net cash rising to ~$2.1B by 2030); the 2025 published GAAP year leaves a -$92M residual (elevated post-valuation-allowance effective tax and undecomposed charges) flagged for the next 10-K pass - the FY2024 GAAP year (net > EBIT, tax benefit) is the known distortion in the historical conversion ratio. Scorecard: anchor FY26 posed at $6.21 (initial >=25% floor). Pre-FY26 the company guided annual REVENUE (not EPS): FY25 initial +19-22% cc vs +29.5% realized = +7.5% level beat, recorded with the metric mismatch declared; application suspended until a same-metric observation exists (FY26 close). Projections unchanged from 10/08 (guidance-anchored: 2026 raised on hard EPS guidance, 2028-2030 re-acceleration kept prudent). WATCH-LIST: (1) Type 2 90-day retention trend; (2) US growth vs 17-19% band; (3) 2027 framing evolution vs the 9-14% initial range; (4) 10-K split of the 2025 bridge residual; (5) competitive entries assumed in 2027 guidance. Next useful refresh: Q3 2026 results (early November).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 2026 results (early Nov): first read on Type 2 remediation; any 2027 range update.

ancrages.moteur: FY26 adjusted EPS guidance explicitly MAINTAINED at +30% minimum vs FY2025 (official base 4,97$) despite the revenue guidance cut - a direct and reliable anchor (hard guidance, confirmed on the call despite the negative backdrop) => omniumEPS 2026 6,46$.

FY26 US Omnipod guidance cut to +17-19% cc, mechanism now specified by the CFO: ~2/3 persistent Type 2 retention/utilization, ~1/3 slower start-up + price phasing, explicitly not competition - an execution risk that is characterised and bounded rather than a diffuse one.
FY26 International guidance raised to +30-32% cc (vs +26-28%), +33% cc in Q2, Australia #1, Spain entry - offsets a significant part of the US decline in absolute terms.

First CFO indication for 2027 (2026 exit 'mid-teens', range 9%/12%/14%, with no retention benefit built in) structurally more prudent than the trajectory adopted at creation - omniumCA/omniumEBIT/omniumEPS 2027-2030 revised down accordingly, growth moderating towards 15-18%/yr rather than the faster reacceleration initially anticipated.

Adjusted operating margin expansion of ~100bp/yr maintained for FY26 despite the revenue trim, slowing gradually to ~80bp/yr at the end of the horizon (increasing maturity of the margin, already at 19,3% in Q2 26).
Q1-Q4 2025 (PY) breakdown quantified on the official base (1,02$/1,17$/1,23$/1,55$): Q4 well above Q3 - pattern carried over for the estimated Q3/Q4 26 split.

The CFO explicitly denies any pricing exclusivity strategy in the Q&A (question on a Blue Cross rollback affecting tubed-pump competitors) - aggressive commercial practice risk/reputational risk ruled out, US prices stable to slightly higher. Drives no adjXXX (an event that is qualitative in nature/a risk ruled out, not a quantifiable projection driver) - nonetheless kept here rather than in the text in order to explicitly track the source id of the watch item.
